title: Severe acute malnutrition
dagger_note: † = clinical or local addition, not in the SA SAM guideline
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold, k=kind (check|value|yn|info|sub), h=heading

admission.title: Diagnostic criteria — any one confirms SAM

items.t: Weight ____ kg · Length ____ cm · MUAC ____ cm
Failed or uncertain RUTF appetite test
Last vitamin A dose within 30 days
Duration of weight loss, oedema onset, appetite

admission.title: Vitals and anthropometry
admission.note: Abnormal = outside age-appropriate norms or the child's baseline

items.t: Baseline liver span noted (to monitor for fluid overload)
< 4 g/dL, or 4–6 g/dL with respiratory distress: transfuse per protocol

admission.title: Red flags to rule out on arrival

items.t: Corneal signs of vitamin A deficiency

decision.t: 11. ADMIT — stabilise, then follow the Days 1–14 chart and the 24-hour nursing record

chart.phase_note: Transition starts when criteria are met, not on a fixed day

standing.t: Weight at the same time daily, plotted
HGT 3-hourly until normal and stable for 24 h
Oedema grade · stimulation and play · caregiver lodging and counselling

rows.label: Day 1
rows.lead: Check the referral note and RtHB for pre-referral doses (vitamin A, antibiotic, F-75, dextrose) — do not repeat vitamin A.

feed.t: 11 mL/kg 2-hourly ×12 if danger signs, hypothermia or hypoglycaemia
NGT if < 80% of the feed is taken

tests.t: HGT on arrival, then 3-hourly (2-hourly if < 3, until ≥ 3 for 24 h)
Blood culture — do not delay antibiotics
VBG + lactate if shock, acidotic breathing or reduced LOC
HIV test: PCR if < 18 mo; any positive < 2 y confirmed on 2nd PCR; ≥ 2 y 2nd rapid test
Mother's HIV status; maternal VL if on ART
TB (SAM = risk of TB): gastric aspirate/sputum for Xpert + TB culture, TST, CXR

treatment.t: Asymptomatic: F-75, or sugar water 5 mL/kg PO, or 50 mL 10% dextrose
Symptomatic: 10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV. Recheck in 30 min
Skin-to-skin, temperature every 30 min
Oxygen, normal saline 10 mL/kg over 10 min, reassess, repeat up to ×4
Stop if overloaded; REFER if > 40 mL/kg needed
ORS 5 mL/kg every 15 min for 4 h
IV ½-Darrow's / 5% DW only if oral fails
Packed cells 5–10 mL/kg over 4 h, furosemide 1 mg/kg at start and end
Antibiotics, vitamin A and supplements: see Doses
Measles (6 and 12 mo) and EPI catch-up if due
Continue cotrimoxazole / ART if already on
No iron, steroids or antidiarrhoeals

tests.t: HGT 3-hourly — stop once normal and stable for 24 h, unless severely ill
VBG only if Day 1 abnormal or deteriorating

treatment.t: Ampicillin IV → oral amoxicillin 30 mg/kg 8-hourly after 2 days; gentamicin to Day 7
Vitamin A dose 2 if eye signs or complicated measles
Watch for fluid overload

feed.t: If oedema reducing, appetite back, active:
F-100 at the same volume as F-75 (transition day 1)

tests.t: U&E + Mg + PO₄ if previously abnormal
If HIV+ (ART baseline): CD4 + FBC; ALT if on TB Rx; creatinine/eGFR if on TDF
Read TST at 48 h (positive: > 10 mm, or > 5 mm if HIV+)

treatment.t: Look for new infection, change to ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg daily
Xpert/culture positive = confirmed
Symptoms + contact, TST+ or CXR = probable: treat, notify, trace contacts
Exposed only: INH 6 months
ART deferred until stabilisation complete

tests.t: U&E + Mg + PO₄ 24–48 h after starting F-100

treatment.t: Correct low K, Mg or PO₄
Hold the feed advance if they are falling — see Doses: refeeding

feed.t: Increase F-100 by 10 mL per feed until some is left over (transition day 3)

treatment.t: Not improving after 5 days of antibiotics: consult or refer

tests.t: U&E + Mg + PO₄ if Day 4 was abnormal

treatment.t: Continue. Maternal counselling with the dietician

tests.t: CRP if sepsis has not clearly resolved

treatment.t: Antibiotics complete (7 days)
Iron 2 mg/kg elemental 8-hourly with meals — only once gaining weight, oedema resolved, not on RUTF
Deworm if ≥ 1 y (see Doses)
Start ART if HIV+ and stabilised; cotrimoxazole

feed.t: Reduce to 5 once eating the ward diet

treatment.t: Weight-gain target > 10 g/kg/d
The 5-day discharge clock starts
Stimulation and play · continue iron
Stop iron once on full RUTF — iron is already in RUTF

tests.t: LFT if on TB treatment with jaundice, vomiting or hepatomegaly

treatment.t: Review TB and ART tolerance
RUTF use, feeding, hygiene, danger signs
Assess the mother's own nutrition if the child is < 2 y (NSP)

tests.t: Repeat TST if the first was negative

treatment.t: Grants (SRD, CSG) · food-security links
Confirm the HIV result is recorded and ART started if positive
EPI complete · RtHB clinical summary
Reassess discharge criteria (Doses tab)
Vitamin A dose 3 if eye signs or complicated measles
DHIS tally · link to PHC and CHW

items.t: REFER TO TERTIARY (guideline regimen: ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg daily × 7 d)
Ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV 6-hourly × 2 days, then amoxicillin 30 mg/kg 8-hourly
Mebendazole: 1–2 y 100 mg BD × 3 days; > 2 y 500 mg stat
Or albendazole: 1–2 y 100 mg stat; > 2 y 200 mg stat

items.h: Vitamin A — all new SAM; defer if a prophylactic dose was given in the last 30 days

items.t: Eye signs or complicated measles: Days 1, 2 and 14

items.h: Commercial F-75, or kitchen F-75 with CMVC

items.t: Folic acid 2.5 mg on Day 1 only
No extra K, Mg, Zn or multivitamin
Magnesium; zinc (< 10 kg 10 mg, > 10 kg 20 mg)
Folic acid 2.5 mg daily; multivitamin 5 mL daily × 14 days or until RUTF
Pulse up by ≥ 25 · RR up by ≥ 5 (from the child's baseline)
Hypothermia, or a sudden temperature rise
HGT · VBG + lactate · U&E + Mg + PO₄ · FBC · CRP · blood culture
If K, Mg or PO₄ fall on feed advance: hold, replace, recheck 24 h
Watch for heart failure, arrhythmia, weakness

discharge.title: Discharge criteria — all six must be met

items.t: > 10 g/kg/d weight gain for 5 consecutive days
TB and HIV ruled out / treatment initiated
Review at 7 days, then weekly until stable, then monthly for at least 2 months
Refer back if oedema returns, weight loss > 5%, static weight over 3 visits, or the appetite test fails

nursing.title: 24-hour nursing record — HGT, weight and feeds
nursing.period: One sheet per 24 hours; hourly rows, heavier rule every 3 h

items.t: Stop once normal and stable for 24 h, unless severely ill
Weigh at the same time each day
Enter g/kg/d in the totals strip
NGT if < 80% of the feed is taken

call.t: Call the doctor for HGT < 3 mmol/L, hypothermia, refusal of feeds, or rising oedema
